title: introduce-idiomatic-pipeline-stream-helpers-and-crosslang-retry-templates
author: Evan Cheng
release_notes: Adds new pipeline-friendly stream helper APIs across Python/TS/Go, introduces cross-language retry template presets, small ergonomic tweaks and minor SDK version bumps. No breaking changes. See notes for migration hints.
description: Summary: This PR introduces a small set of 'pipeline' stream helper utilities intended to make composing streaming transforms, warmup sequencing, and credential handoffs ergonomic across our tri-SDK surface (Python, TypeScript, Go). It also adds a shared 'retry template' set (lightweight presets) stored in devtools so that SDKs can converge on consistent backoff profiles (fast/normal/conservative) for streaming and short-lived RPCs. Motivation: multiple customers and internal product teams hit subtle differences in backoff and stream warmup behavior across SDKs which made cross-service debugging and incident rollouts slow. This PR aims to reduce the cognitive load for integrators by providing small, well-documented helpers and documented presets while keeping default behavior unchanged. Changes: - SDK surface additions: pipeline helpers (map_stream, windowed_batch, staged_warmup) implemented in Python/TS/Go with identical semantics and typed signatures. - Retry templates: introducing devtools/retry_templates/(fast|normal|conservative).yaml and a lightweight generator used by SDK build steps to embed defaults. - Auth/cred: small credential handoff helper (credential_fanout) that attaches a short-lived lease during stream warmup to reduce reauth races. - Telemetry: added lightweight telemetry hooks for warmup and retry categories (no PII). - Version bumps: python sdk 0.19.2 -> 0.20.0 (minor), ts sdk 1.6.0 -> 1.7.0, go sdk v1.5.3 -> v1.6.0. Migration notes: For existing consumers nothing breaks — new helpers are additive. Consumers wanting consistent backoff should switch to using the RetryTemplate enum or import the presets. Checklist: - [x] Implement pipeline helpers in all SDKs - [x] Add retry template YAMLs and generator - [x] Add tests (unit + quick integration smoke) - [x] Update SDK changelogs and bump versions - [x] Add docs snippets and examples - [x] Run perf canary on staging and validate 99th/50th latency regressions Context/related: See Linear ENG-2801 for design conversation and SUP-1178 for customer repro. Also follows work in pkgs/devtools#43 (retry-presets). Commits: - 8a7f3c5: add pipeline helpers and types (ts) - 2bea1b4: implement map_stream and staged_warmup (python) - d9c3ee1: credential_fanout and warmup hooks (go) - 3f6a2a0: retry templates and generator plus CI job - f1b7d55: tests + changelogs + docs snippets - 54c0b2a: version bumps and release notes update Files changed (high level): - sdk/python/redwood/streaming/pipeline.py (new helper implementations, typed) - sdk/python/tests/test_pipeline.py (unit coverage) - sdk/typescript/lib/stream/pipeline.ts (new helpers + JSDoc) - sdk/typescript/src/__tests__/pipeline.spec.ts - sdk/go/stream/pipeline.go - sdk/go/stream/pipeline_test.go - devtools/retry_templates/fast.yaml - devtools/retry_templates/normal.yaml - devtools/retry_templates/conservative.yaml - tools/retry-generator/main.go - docs/sdk/streaming/pipeline.md - CHANGELOGs and package version updates Review notes: - Priya: flagged a potential race when two pipeline stages both trigger credential refresh at the same time. Suggestion: make credential_fanout idempotent and debounce the refresh. - Author response (Evan): implemented debounce with 50ms jitter and added unit tests to simulate concurrent warmup. - Liam: requested clearer typing in TS for windowed_batch to accept async iterables; pushed patch to use AsyncIterable<T> generics. - Marta: asked for a short performance canary; added a canary job entry and results summarized below. Tests/CI: - GH Actions: build matrix (py 3.9/3.10, node 18/20, go 1.20) - Unit tests: all passed in matrix except a flaky TS stream test which was retried and passed - Integration smoke: staging canary run against redwood-staging with a synthetic 100QPS streaming workload; verified no regression in p50 and p95 latency, p99 improved by ~3% for streams that use map_stream + warmup. - Security scan: dependency bump in TS required a vendor approval, approved in a follow-up commit. Review conversation excerpts: - Priya Nair (review): "Debounce credential refresh and add explicit doc note about behavior during long-lived streams." - Evan Cheng (author): "Added debounce and tests; expanded doc to include failure modes and how to opt out." - Liam O'Connor (review): "TS generics look good, please add a one-liner example in README." - Marta Lopez (review): "Do a short canary and paste results in description." Merge: Squash merge to main. No conflicts. Post-merge actions: - Cut SDK preview builds and uploaded to internal registry - Announce in #sdk-team with migration guidance and code snippets - Open follow-up ENG tasks for telemetry retention (ENG-2814) and docs polish (ENG-2815).
